title: Few Tokens, Big Leverage: Preserving Safety Alignment by Constraining Safety Tokens during Fine-tuning

problem.claim: Fine-tuning can cause safety-alignment drift and weaken refusal behavior, including when training data is benign.

gap.claim: Existing defenses use model-wide restrictions or additional safety data, which can reduce generality and downstream task performance.

contributions.claim: PACT is a fine-tuning framework that preserves safety alignment by constraining confidence on safety-related tokens.
PACT matches the fine-tuned model's confidence on safety-related tokens to an aligned reference model while leaving non-safety tokens largely unconstrained.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an empirical observation that safety-aligned behavior is reflected in token-level output confidence and concentrated on a small subset of safety-related tokens.
The authors state that the targeted constraint prevents alignment drift without imposing global restrictions that trade off with model utility.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fine-tuning can induce safety-alignment drift and compromise refusal behavior.
Model-wide defense strategies may constrain generality and harm downstream performance.
PACT preserves confidence on safety-related tokens during downstream fine-tuning.
The targeted constraint is intended to prevent alignment drift while retaining task adaptation.
Implementation code is reported as publicly available.

source_observation.claim: Safety behavior may be concentrated in a small subset of output tokens.

interpretation.claim: Targeting safety-relevant token confidence may preserve safety behavior with less interference in general task adaptation.

application.claim: For safety-preserving fine-tuning, constrain safety-related output signals while leaving other token predictions more flexible.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this targeted strategy works across models, tasks, or safety distributions.

unknowns: No models, datasets, tasks, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are specified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the claimed prevention of alignment drift.
The definition of safety-related tokens and the regularization objective are unspecified.
